articles.summary: NVIDIA and Bilkent University researchers adopt TQT as their quantized retraining method, stating "we use TQT [25] as our baseline retraining method" (p. 5) and crediting it with "state-of-the-art results for several networks" (p. 1). They train thresholds in the log domain and follow the five-epoch schedule of [25], noting implementation differences (pp. 4–6), report accuracy before and after TQT (Table I, p. 6), contrast results without TQT (p. 7) and in the conclusion describe "a state-of-the-art TQT quantized retraining method" (p. 9).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.
articles.authors: Sukru Burc Eryilmaz; Aysegul Dundar

articles.summary: Sony researchers implement TQT as the fixed-bitwidth benchmark for their mixed-precision method, learning qmax at a fixed 2-bit width "as was done in (Jain et al., 2019)" and reporting the "TQT" configuration in their CIFAR-10 and ImageNet tables (pp. 8–9). They credit Jain et al., in work parallel to their own, with learning the quantizer's dynamic range through the straight-through estimator (p. 2) and cite it for the power-of-two step size that efficient hardware requires (p. 4).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained uniform quantization for accurate and efficient neural network inference on fixed-point hardware.

articles.summary: University of California, Santa Cruz and Intel researchers adopt TQT's threshold training in the quantization of their 4-bit QW-Net image-reconstruction network, stating "Following Jain et al. [2019], we train the thresholds in log space" to improve stability with quantized training (Section 5.1, p. 6). The article explains that Jain et al. and Esser et al. showed that quantization thresholds could be trained to improve accuracy, with a straight-through-estimator gradient that lets thresholds grow for dynamic range or shrink for precision (p. 3). The log-space training is attributed to Jain et al. alone.
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.
articles.authors: Manu Mathew Thomas; Karthik Vaidyanathan; Gabor Liktor; Angus G. Forbes

articles.summary: Researchers in the ETH Zürich/University of Bologna PULP group quantize their tiny transformers for low-power microcontrollers with TQT, stating "We use the uniform symmetric quantizer from the SotA [state-of-the-art] Trained Quantization Threshold (TQT) method [3]", and specify the functional behavior of the TQT quantizer in their deployment flow (Section IV-C, p. 6). The introduction also cites TQT for data quantization among standard hardware-agnostic optimization techniques (p. 1).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.
articles.authors: Victor J.B. Jung; Alessio Burrello; Moritz Scherer; Francesco Conti; Luca Benini

articles.summary: KU Leuven researchers take TQT as the starting point of their work: crediting Jain et al. with having "already proved" that 8-bit models with power-of-two scales reach full-precision accuracy, they set out to extend this to 4-bit weights (pp. 2, 14). They adopt its method, optimizing power-of-two scales "as proposed by Jain et al." (p. 12) with its quantizer, hyperparameters and scale freezing (p. 17), and extend its freezing to per-channel scales, finding its "per-layer results were consistent with ours" (p. 19). Table 2 lists TQT as the only prior power-of-two-scale method, within 1.6 points of full precision at 4-bit weights (p. 20).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.
articles.authors: Maarten Vandersteegen; Kristof Van Beeck; Toon Goedemé

articles.summary: ETH Zürich and University of Bologna researchers train their ternarized gesture-recognition networks with two quantization-aware training algorithms, INQ and TQT (p. 6). They use TQT to learn weight and activation clipping bounds (pp. 5–6), specify its hyperparameters (Table 3, p. 9) and train their Pareto-front networks with it (p. 9). They report that "the combination of ReLU activations and TQT yields the highest classification accuracy", ahead of INQ (Table 4, p. 10).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

articles.summary: Qualcomm researchers adapt the procedure of Esser et al. and Jain et al. to learn the ranges of both weights and activations in their quantization-aware training of BERT-like transformer models (p. 7), having noted that such ranges can be learned jointly with the weights during training "as in Esser et al. (2019); Jain et al. (2019)" (p. 3).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained uniform quantization for accurate and efficient neural network inference on fixed-point hardware.

articles.summary: Inha University and Sangmyung University researchers identify LSQ and TQT as "the current state-of-the-art quantization methods" (p. 6) and develop log level threshold quantization (LLTQ) from TQT's power-of-two scale mapping: LLTQ maps the trainable parameter directly to a power-of-two scale and replaces TQT's pre-calibration with first-batch statistics (pp. 3–4, 6). They illustrate and train LSQ, TQT and LLTQ (pp. 7, 10) and report TQT as hardware-friendly but about 0.45% below floating-point accuracy, a gap LLTQ closes (pp. 11–12).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

articles.summary: EPFL, Sony and University of Padova researchers report that their most effective uniform-precision quantization-aware training procedure initializes from the pretrained float32 model and uses "learnable qmax as in the Trained Quantization Threshold (TQT) approach [23]", stabilized with cosine learning-rate decay and RMSprop followed by Adam (Section 5.1, p. 5). The related-work section cites TQT among recent quantization-aware training methods that "proved effective on classification tasks" (p. 2).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

articles.summary: Seoul National University and Qualcomm researchers state that LSQ [8] and TQT [17] "introduce uniform quantization using trainable interval values" and that "Our QKD leverages these trainable approaches in the baseline quantization implementation" (p. 2), introducing trainable interval parameters for each layer's weights and input activations similar to [8, 17, 45] (p. 3). They also cite TQT on the quantization sensitivity of depthwise convolutions (p. 7). Knowledge distillation is applied on top of this baseline, so the reported results reflect the combined method.
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.
articles.authors: Jangho Kim; Yash Bhalgat; Jinwon Lee; Chirag Patel; Nojun Kwak

articles.summary: Xilinx researchers in Beijing build bin regularization on a hardware-friendly quantization baseline that they re-implement following references [19, 21], where [19] is TQT: power-of-two step sizes, low-bit first and last layers, quantized inputs and outputs of element-wise additions, 8-bit biases and batch normalization merged during training (p. 8). Table 9 reports 63.8% top-1 accuracy for TQT, 65.8% for TQT+L2 and 67.5% for TQT+BR on 4-bit MobileNetV2, which the text describes as "+3.7% over TQT" (p. 8). The authors are affiliated with Xilinx Inc.; the entry is employer-linked.
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.
articles.authors: Tiantian Han; Dong Li; Ji Liu; Lu Tian; Yi Shan

articles.summary: Qualcomm AI Research authors credit reference [15], the TQT paper, together with LSQ [8], with having "independently introduced" the learning of the quantization scale along with the model parameters for a fixed-bitwidth network; both papers, they explain, expose the scale parameter to the learning process so that it is optimized jointly with the network's parameters (p. 6). Figure 2b compares Bayesian Bits on MobileNetV2 with AdaRound, LSQ and TQT (p. 8).

articles.summary: Snap Inc., Northeastern University and Rice University researchers define F8Net against the fixed-point quantization of Jain et al. (2019), which uses trainable power-of-two scale factors to replace multiplication with bit shifting, stating that their work "differs from previous efforts (Jain et al., 2019) in three major aspects" (p. 2). They contrast F8Net's on-the-fly fractional length with TQT's directly trained fractional length (p. 7) and compare with TQT in Table 1 for MobileNet V1 and V2b, reporting that their approach gives better results (p. 8).

articles.summary: University of Granada-led researchers use TQT in the quantization-aware training of their AMD DPU implementation for configuring reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, stating "For the quantization strategy, a power-of-two scale quantizer with training quantization threshold (TQT) was used [50]" (Section 3.2, p. 9). TQT is applied together with activation and training refinements, so the reported results reflect the combined pipeline.

articles.summary: Robert Bosch GmbH, Fraunhofer IPMS and University of Kaiserslautern researchers evaluate the classification accuracy of their ferroelectric-FET in-memory accelerator with 8-bit/4-bit (input/weight) quantization "based on the optimizations presented in [17]", the TQT paper (Section 6.2, p. 17).

articles.summary: Sony Semiconductor Israel researchers cite references [24, 41] for hardware-friendly quantizers that are per-tensor, uniform, symmetric and use power-of-two thresholds, and describe these properties as "an imperative requirement for many efficient edge device hardware implementations" with reference to [24], the TQT paper (p. 2). They state that the quantizer used in HMQ "is similar to the one in [24]" before defining its signed and unsigned forms (p. 4).

articles.summary: In the related-work discussion of AdaRound, Qualcomm researchers credit Esser et al. and Jain et al. with learning the quantization minimum and maximum ranges during training "so that they do not have to be set manually" (p. 5). AdaRound is a post-training rounding method and does not itself apply TQT; the entry rests on the article's venue and citation count.

articles.summary: Qualcomm's white paper on neural network quantization credits Esser et al., Jain et al. and Bhalgat et al. with using the straight-through estimator to calculate the gradient with respect to the quantization parameters, and then develops the gradient derivation for the scale factor (p. 20). It also cites Jain et al. among works that start quantization-aware training from a pretrained FP32 model, which it calls "common practice in literature" (p. 22).

articles.summary: This Neurocomputing survey by Nanyang Technological University researchers, conducted in collaboration with HP Inc. (p. 1), lists TQT among 8-bit quantization techniques for weights and activations in its comparison table (p. 8) and summarizes Jain et al.'s trained uniform quantization method for accurate and efficient inference on fixed-point hardware (p. 9). The survey describes the method without reporting use of it; the entry rests on the survey's citation count.

articles.summary: Kyushu Institute of Technology researchers quantize the activations of their ITBWN networks to INT8 with TQT while using binary or ternary weights (pp. 3–4). They describe TQT's removal of the zero point, its power-of-two scale and its threshold training with the straight-through estimator (p. 2), and report that INT8 activations from TQT or BinaryConnect allow the weight-quantized models to deploy without the cost of floating-point accumulation (p. 5). They use the default TQT implementation in Xilinx Brevitas, which they describe as having "minor differences with the TQT settings": no power-of-two scale and a different scale initialization (p. 3).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

articles.summary: The Alan Turing Institute researchers deploy a YOLOv8-based SAR vessel detector on an AMD/Xilinx Kria KV260 FPGA, quantizing it to INT8 with the Vitis AI Quantizer using symmetric power-of-two scaling; the sentence describing post-training quantization and quantization-aware training (QAT) "using a straight-through estimator" cites reference [35], the TQT paper (p. 5). They retrain with a tuned quantizer-parameter learning rate (Section 4.2.2) and report that the deployed QAT models match the expected GPU performance with little to no degradation (Table 4, Section 4.3, p. 11). The article does not state which Vitis AI QAT mode was used, and the use came through the AMD/Xilinx Vitis AI toolchain.
